chunks: Al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Muhammad, and I heard it from Ali, who said:
I wrote to him: 'Does a loan (qard) that draws benefit, is it permissible or not?' He wrote back to me with peace: 'That is permissible.'

And I wrote to him: 'A man has a debt of dates, or wheat, or barley, or cotton against another man. When they settled the debt, he said: Take the value of what is with me in dirhams. Is that permissible for him or not?' He wrote back to him with peace: 'That is permissible by mutual consent of both, if God wills.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay back a loan of goods with money or a different good?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a loan (qard) may include a benefit for the lender, addressing early juristic debates on whether such附加 conditions invalidate the gratuitous nature of the loan. It further establishes the permissibility of settling a debt in kind with a different commodity or currency, provided there is mutual consent (taradhin) between the parties, reflecting the flexibility of Shia commercial jurisprudence in debt settlement.
